steps.name: Prepare gene lists and universe from DE results
steps.question: From de_results.csv (12000 genes, treated vs control DESeq2 contrast), how many genes pass the adjusted-p threshold, what is the full ranked list of tested genes by the Wald statistic, and what is the background universe for enrichment?
steps.description: Load /eval-full-32-with-gene-list-ora-2/data/inputs/results/de_results.csv. Report the number of genes with padj < 0.05 (the significant list for ORA) and confirm whether it meets or falls short of the ~50-gene power threshold for over-representation testing. Build (a) the significant gene symbol list at padj<0.05, (b) the full ranked list of all 12000 tested genes ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the 'stat' column; state this choice explicitly since the ranking metric is a disputed parameter), and (c) the universe = all 12000 tested gene symbols. Map gene symbols to Entrez IDs using org.Hs.eg.db, report the fraction of genes that fail to map or map ambiguously, and drop unmapped/many-to-one duplicates with a stated count. Save the significant list, ranked list, and universe as intermediate files for the enrichment step.
acceptance_criteria: Reports the count of significant genes (padj<0.05) and explicitly states whether it is above or below 50
Reports the percentage of gene symbols that failed to map to Entrez IDs via org.Hs.eg.db
Produces three saved artifacts: significant gene list, full ranked list (by DESeq2 stat), and universe list, all in Entrez ID space with symbol lookup retained

steps.name: GO Biological Process over-representation analysis (ORA)
steps.question: Which GO Biological Process terms are over-represented among the genes significant (padj<0.05) in the AD lesional vs control contrast, using all 12000 tested genes as the statistical background?
steps.description: Run clusterProfiler::enrichGO on the significant gene list from T1S1 against ontology='BP', using org.Hs.eg.db for annotation, with the universe explicitly set to the full list of tested genes (not the whole genome). Restrict to gene sets with 15-500 members among the tested genes. Adjust p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg. If the reference GO:BP gene set collection (MSigDB C5 GO:BP symbols GMT, expected under a pathways reference store) is present, cross-check the enrichGO result against an equivalent clusterProfiler::enricher() run on that GMT to confirm consistency; if enrichGO's built-in GO.db/org.Hs.eg.db annotation is sufficient, that alone is acceptable since it is the standard-practice route for GO ORA. Reduce the significant BP terms (adjusted p<0.05) to non-redundant representative terms using rrvgo semantic similarity (org.Hs.eg.db as the OrgDb, ontology='BP'). Save both the full enrichGO results table and the rrvgo-reduced representative-term table.
acceptance_criteria: enrichGO run with ontology=BP, universe=tested genes (not whole genome), pAdjustMethod=BH, gene set size window 15-500
Full GO:BP ORA results table saved with GO ID, term name, gene ratio, bg ratio, p-value, padj, and member genes
rrvgo-reduced non-redundant representative term table saved alongside the full table
If fewer than ~50 genes were significant (per T1S1), this is stated as a caveat on the ORA result's reliability

steps.name: Complementary GO:BP preranked GSEA on the full gene list
steps.question: Independent of a hard significance cutoff, which GO Biological Process gene sets show coordinated enrichment across the full ranked list of tested genes in the AD lesional vs control contrast?
steps.description: Run a preranked GSEA (fgsea, via clusterProfiler::GSEA or fgsea directly) against the GO Biological Process collection using the full ranked list of all 12000 tested genes from T1S1, ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic ('stat' column — the same metric named in T1S1, chosen because it scales effect size by its uncertainty rather than using the unshrunken log2FC alone or a signed p-value with ties). Use the MSigDB GO:BP gene sets GMT reference for human (the c5.go.bp symbols file under the pathways reference store) restricted to sets with 15-500 members among the tested genes, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. This step exists because a hard padj cutoff on a modest DE list can miss small coordinated shifts that ORA cannot detect; report the overlap and disagreement between this ranked result and the T1S2 ORA result explicitly, per standard practice that enrichment methods disagree and neither is a proven finding on its own. Report leading-edge genes for each significant gene set.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea/GSEA run on the full ranked list (all 12000 genes), not a thresholded subset
Ranking metric explicitly stated as the DESeq2 Wald statistic
GO:BP gene sets restricted to 15-500 members among tested genes, BH-adjusted
Leading-edge genes reported for each significant (padj<0.05) gene set
Overlap/disagreement between this GSEA result and the T1S2 ORA result is explicitly compared and reported

steps.name: Consolidated GO biological process enrichment report
steps.question: What is the consolidated, caveated answer to which GO biological processes are over-represented in the AD lesional vs control comparison, combining the ORA and the ranked-GSEA evidence?
steps.description: Combine the T1S2 ORA table (with rrvgo-reduced representative terms) and the T1S3 ranked-GSEA table into a single report. State explicitly: the GO:BP gene set database and its version, the universe used (tested genes, n=12000), the gene set size window (15-500), the ranking metric used for GSEA (DESeq2 Wald statistic), the number of genes significant at padj<0.05 feeding the ORA and whether that count met the ~50-gene threshold needed for ORA to have power, the BH multiple-testing correction, and the fraction of gene symbols unmapped to Entrez. State that ORA and ranked GSEA are different methods that can disagree, and report which representative BP terms are corroborated by both versus found by only one. Note the caveat that sample_01 (already reflected in the upstream DE results) had a library size ~4x below the median, which widens its per-gene uncertainty but was not deleted, per the DE results this analysis inherits. Include a reproducibility record: package versions (clusterProfiler, org.Hs.eg.db, GO.db, rrvgo, fgsea), the GO:BP collection version, and the random seed used in any permutation-based step (fgsea).
acceptance_criteria: Report lists representative non-redundant GO:BP terms with padj, gene counts, and member genes for both ORA and GSEA results
Report explicitly states database version, universe, size window, ranking metric, and multiple-testing method
Report states whether the significant gene list met the 50-gene ORA power threshold
Report includes a reproducibility record with package versions and any random seed used
Report notes agreement/disagreement between ORA and GSEA results as two distinct pieces of evidence, not a single unified finding

plan.title: AD lesional vs control GO biological process ORA
plan.analytical_narrative: The input already carries a DESeq2 results table for the treated (AD lesional) vs control skin contrast (12000 genes tested, 6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch). The research question is specifically about GO biological processes over-represented among the significant genes, so the core method is a GO:BP over-representation analysis (ORA) on the significant gene list, using clusterProfiler::enrichGO with the full set of tested genes as the statistical universe (never the whole genome, per bias-correction practice) and org.Hs.eg.db for symbol-to-Entrez mapping. Because ORA on a short significant list has essentially no power below ~50 genes (a documented failure mode), the plan first counts how many genes pass padj<0.05 and, if that number is small, still runs the ORA (since that is what was asked) but adds a parallel fgsea preranked GSEA against the same GO:BP collection on the full ranked gene list as a complementary, higher-power method, explicitly reporting both so a small/underpowered ORA result is not overclaimed. GO terms nest heavily, so significant BP terms are reduced to non-redundant representative terms with rrvgo before reporting, and the full unreduced table is kept as a supplement. The report step consolidates both analyses, states the universe, gene set size window (15-500), database version, ranking metric, redundancy collapse, and reproducibility record (package versions, seed), and flags the caveats: the ORA method-dependence, the sample_01 low-depth caveat already baked into the supplied DE results, and whether the significant list met the 50-gene power threshold.

steps.method: clusterProfiler enrichGO (GO Biological Process) with rrvgo redundancy reduction, on genes with padj<0.05 from de_results.csv, universe = all tested genes
fgsea preranked GSEA on DESeq2 Wald statistic against GO:BP (fallback/complement when significant gene list is small)
Enrichment report with database version, universe, rank metric, size window, redundancy collapse, leading edge genes
